aoi.note: Bounded Carlisle screening envelope. It is frozen for source discovery only; a modelling grid and hydraulic domain have not yet been asserted.

domainEnvelope.note: The envelope extends the source-discovery AOI east only far enough to contain Great Corby. It freezes the input protocol footprint, not channel placement, cell size or a runnable hydraulic mesh.

downstreamBoundary.requiredEvidence: event-valid stage, discharge, rating relation or normal-depth condition in a declared vertical datum

initialState.note: The first four discharge samples do not define channel stage, floodplain wetness or a distributed initial condition.

datasets.publisher: NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center
datasets.dataset: GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 Half Hourly 0.1 degree x 0.1 degree V07
datasets.license: NASA GPM data policy; source acknowledgement requested

access.note: The canonical Python earthaccess path found every expected V07 Final Run granule without opening or downloading the rasters. V07 is retrospective reprocessing and was not available during the 2015 event.

datasets.sourceResolution: 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m or 2 m depending on survey

access.note: The official catalogue proves exact source dates for 231 bounded 1 km grid references and leaves ten explicitly missing. The current survey search maps every selected source row to one of 30 official 5 km time-stamped DTM ZIP identities; a bounded header-only probe verified the NY3555 sample as application/zip without reading archive bytes.

lidarCatalogAudit.selectionRule: per OS grid reference: latest surveyEnd before event window; then smallest point spacing; then smallest objectId

downloadMapping.mappingRule: map each selected 1 km OS grid reference to its containing 5 km tile; require the selected survey-end year; choose the smallest advertised DTM raster resolution; then URI
downloadMapping.materializationRule: accept raster pixels only inside the selected 1 km grid references mapped to each archive; the containing 5 km archive does not make every pixel event-valid

lidarCatalogAudit.reason: All 231 selected pre-event source rows map to 30 official 5 km DTM archive identities. Ten grid references still have no pre-event source record and must remain missing; no raster archive has been downloaded by this audit.

datasets.sourceResolution: 100 m raster; 25 ha minimum mapping unit
datasets.license: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service data policy

access.note: Reference imagery is 2011-2012, before Storm Desmond. The currently published corrected release is post-event retrospective processing and is disclosed as such.

datasets.sourceResolution: generalised connected river links and nodes
datasets.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 with Ordnance Survey attribution

access.note: The current product confirms open hydrography access but is not yet an as-of-December-2015 network edition. It remains context-only until historical lineage is frozen.

datasets.sourceResolution: WFD-designated subset of the CEH 1:50,000 river network
datasets.license: Open Government Licence with Environment Agency, CEH and Ordnance Survey attribution

access.note: The bounded WFS query returns 16 event-valid WFD water bodies. Intersecting source geometries are returned whole rather than clipped to the AOI. This is a historically valid river context layer, not a complete channel, defence or hydraulic network.

hydrographyAudit.blocker: The dataset includes only WFD-designated 1:50,000 river stretches and is not a complete channel or hydraulic network.

access.note: The public API returned a complete 72-hour qualified series directly on the River Eden at Carlisle. It is frozen as observation comparison, not calibration or a silent model boundary.

datasets.dataset: Hydrology API qualified instantaneous water level

access.note: The public API returned a complete 72-hour qualified series at Sheepmount. Gauge level is retained in station-local semantics and is not interpreted as water depth.
The complete local Carlisle gauge series is observation comparison only. Its 49 mm total must not be represented as catchment-wide or high-fell rainfall.

The complete Eden flow series is a candidate upstream hydrograph for a future Carlisle hydraulic domain. Great Corby lies just outside the metadata AOI, so this series cannot define or silently expand the modelling domain by itself.

The complete Irthing flow series is a candidate upstream hydrograph because the official 2011 Carlisle model domain names Greenholme Weir as a separate upstream limit. Station coordinates remain observation locations, not verified model cross-sections.
The complete Caldew flow series is a candidate upstream hydrograph only. It cannot become a boundary condition until the station-to-domain relation, timing and units are frozen.
The complete Petteril flow series is a candidate upstream hydrograph only. It is not a calibrated or inferred hydraulic boundary.

datasets.dataset: AIMS Spatial Flood Defences including standardised attributes
datasets.sourceResolution: current defence line geometry and asset-level attributes

access.note: The bounded OGC query is reproducible, but the source is a daily current inventory. Asset start dates do not make current geometry, crest levels, condition or standards an as-of-2015 defence state.

defenceContextAudit.blocker: The source is current, daily-updated and incomplete for event dating; current geometry, crest and condition attributes cannot reconstruct the defence state on 4 December 2015.

datasets.sourceResolution: current channel and culvert line inventory

access.note: The bounded OGC inventory is reproducible but current and mostly lacks asset start dates. It contains channel and culvert line context, not cross-sections, bed levels or hydraulic roughness, so it cannot be promoted to the 2015 solver geometry.

channelContextAudit.blocker: The source is a current asset inventory, 272 of 349 records have no start date and 17 dated records start on or after the event; the schema contains no cross-section, bed-elevation or roughness fields required for an event-valid hydraulic model.

datasets.dataset: Carlisle SFRA main report and Appendix C
datasets.sourceResolution: public reports describing the historical model domain; no machine-readable model package
datasets.license: Public authority publication; redistribution not assessed

access.note: The reports identify four upstream watercourse limits and Old Sandsfield as the downstream model limit. They establish historical domain lineage only; the named gauging stations are not asserted to equal model cross-sections and no boundary values are attached.

hydraulicDomainLineageAudit.blocker: The reports name the model limits and lineage but do not attach the historical cross-sections, boundary time series, downstream relation, roughness, mesh or executable ISIS/TUFLOW files.

datasets.dataset: Carlisle SFRA Appendix D - Breach Analysis Methodology
datasets.sourceResolution: four-page methodology appendix; no machine-readable model package
datasets.license: Public authority publication; redistribution not assessed

access.note: The pre-event appendix proves that an ISIS 1D and TUFLOW 2D model incorporating the Carlisle defence schemes existed. It describes model lineage and scenarios, not a runnable artifact or event boundary package.

hydraulicModelLineageAudit.blocker: The cited 2008 modelling report, 2010 flood-warning study and ISIS/TUFLOW files are not attached, so the document cannot be executed or converted into inferred geometry.

datasets.sourceResolution: model-footprint polygons and descriptive metadata; no model files or outputs

access.note: The official bounded OGC catalogue returned 19 Carlisle-area model records and now provides exact group identities for a future Environment Agency request. The catalogue still excludes model files and outputs; post-event Carlisle 2015 and 2016 records cannot enter replay input or calibration.

floodModelCatalogAudit.blocker: The catalogue exposes model-group identities and footprints only. The runnable files, outputs, historical cross-sections and event-valid boundary package must still be obtained separately.

access.note: The official OGC Features endpoint returned Carlisle geometry during the audit but was intermittently unavailable on a repeated request. Exact feature identifiers and hashes remain deliberately unfrozen until the input protocol is sealed.

datasets.dataset: EMSR147 Carlisle flood delineation and monitoring
datasets.license: Copernicus Emergency Management Service reuse terms

access.note: Both official Carlisle vector archives returned HTTP 200. They remain sealed evaluation references and have not been downloaded into the repository.

datasets.dataset: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Carlisle, December 2015
datasets.license: Public authority publication; redistribution not assessed

access.note: The report supports event timing and identifies defence overtopping without proving that the current metadata audit has a runnable hydraulic model. It is context-only.

gates.reason: Official Met Office and local investigation sources support a 72-hour UTC audit window covering rainfall onset, peak event and immediate response.
The bounded Carlisle envelope is frozen for source discovery and contains the direct Sheepmount reference station.
The canonical NASA path found 144 of 144 V07 Final Run half-hour granules for the exact window.
Sheepmount flow and level plus Willow Holme rainfall each return all 288 expected 15-minute values.

Great Corby, Greenholme, Cummersdale and Newbiggin Bridge each return all 288 qualified 15-minute flow values for the frozen window. Their identities, units, native sampling and fail-closed treatment are frozen by the local boundary protocol.

The logical local envelope and four upstream discharge identities are frozen without inventing channel placement, interpolation, a downstream condition, an initial state or a hydraulic mesh. Old Sandsfield is retained only as the documented historical model limit because its boundary values remain unavailable.

The official Products 5, 6 and 7 request is frozen for pre-event model groups 1313, 1314, 1797 and 8323. Product 4 and post-event groups 2039 and 9458 are excluded so observed or hindsight material cannot silently enter replay input.
CLC 2012 gives an explicit pre-event reference year while retaining its post-event corrected release identity.
Recorded Flood Outlines and EMSR147 are structurally evaluation-only and cannot enter model input or calibration.

The official catalogue selects 231 dated pre-event 1 km grid references and the current survey search maps all of them to 30 downloadable 5 km DTM ZIP identities. The ten uncovered references remain explicit missing terrain and whole-archive pixels outside the selected 1 km mapping are not event-valid by default.

WFD River Water Bodies Cycle 1 provides 16 event-valid river-context features, but it is a 1:50,000 WFD subset rather than a complete channel or hydraulic network; current OS Open Rivers remains context-only.

The 2011 Carlisle SFRA records an ISIS 1D/TUFLOW 2D model, four upstream watercourse limits, Old Sandsfield downstream, defence schemes and 23 floodgates, but only as document lineage rather than executable evidence.

The bounded AIMS query returns 291 current defences, but 114 lack a start date, 56 start on or after the event and four report post-2015 refurbishment; daily current geometry and crest attributes cannot be represented as the December 2015 state.

The four-series upstream protocol and historical domain lineage are frozen, and six Carlisle model-group identities are known. No runnable ISIS/TUFLOW package, event-valid channel geometry/roughness, downstream condition, distributed initial state or as-of-2015 defence state has been accepted.
Evaluation services are accessible, but exact feature selections and hashes will be frozen only after the input protocol is sealed.

Terrain archive identities and evaluation isolation are now reproducible, but runnable model geometry, boundary placement and values, initial state, defence state and final mesh remain unresolved. No bulk terrain acquisition is needed until those physical gates advance.

acquisition.nextAction: Send the frozen Products 5, 6 and 7 request if it has not already been submitted. While awaiting the response, freeze the bounded 30-archive terrain materialization and content-addressing protocol without downloading rasters; retain ten terrain grid references and every unresolved hydraulic component explicitly missing.
